Compute a small-circle path for a stereonet (radians)

Source: R/dir-utils.R
SmallCircle.Rd

Computes the path(s) of a small circle defined by its rotation axis and cone angle on an equal-area or equal-angle stereonet of unit radius. When the small circle crosses the primitive, the path is split into two segments.

Usage

SmallCircle(trda, plga, coneAngle, wulff = F, closed = F)

Arguments

trda

Numeric. Trend of the rotation axis in radians.

plga

Numeric. Plunge of the rotation axis in radians.

coneAngle

Numeric. Half-apex (cone) angle in radians.

wulff

Logical. If TRUE uses an equal-angle (Wulff) net; if FALSE (default) uses an equal-area (Schmidt) net.

closed

Logical. If TRUE the path segments are closed by appending the first point to the end. Default FALSE.

Value

A named list with components:

path1

Matrix of stereonet coordinates for the main segment.

path2

Matrix of stereonet coordinates for the secondary segment (empty when the circle does not cross the primitive).

References

Allmendinger, R. W., Cardozo, N., & Fisher, D. M. (2012). Structural geology algorithms: Vectors and tensors. Cambridge university press.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Triple colon required because it's not exported
GMisc:::SmallCircle(trda = pi / 4, plga = pi / 6, coneAngle = pi / 8)
} # }
